title: Terminal option payoffs and sampled variance
prompt: All figures and markets in this question are synthetic. Consider two admissible scenario completions of a terminal-only data record; these are possible realized paths, not asserted risk-neutral pricing models. Both start and end at100 over one year, with an observation at half-year. Realized variance is the sum of the two squared log returns divided by one year, with no demeaning or annualization multiplier beyond this definition. All vanilla options here depend only on terminal spot. Return variance for both paths, the absolute difference in terminal payoff of one strike100 European call, and whether the terminal-only record identifies realized variance.

outputs.name: call_payoff_difference
outputs.description: Absolute difference between the two terminal call payoffs.
